The rationale calls the comparison with iteration 0 'clean' because the geometry matches, but the controller differs in four parameters. Iteration 1 showed that a multi-change design cannot be attributed to any one factor, and this draft repeats that problem.

2. The s-bend progress is 0.1475 in both iteration 0 and iteration 1, to four decimal places, even though kp, kd, ki, base_speed, sensor layout, mass and track width all differed. That is strong evidence that the s-bend failure point is set by something the controller changes did not touch, probably the start condition or a fixed feature of the track. This draft does not test that hypothesis, and its changes would not be expected to move that point.

3. The sensor-size arithmetic does not support the stated benefit. A sensor at lateral offset x_s sees tape when |offset - x_s| < 0.0125 + size/2. With size 0.016 and an outer sensor at 0.04, that is an offset window up to about 0.06 m, which is the off-track limit. The robot therefore keeps a reading on the outer sensors almost to the point of leaving the track, so line loss near 0.06 m is expected whatever the footprint. A larger footprint does not stop the drift; it only changes when the sensors start to read. The benefit depends on the controller correcting drift, which this draft does not make stronger in any tested way.

4. The larger footprint also overlaps adjacent sensors more (2 cm spacing, 1.6 cm footprint), so the readings become more correlated. The centre sensors lose resolution on small offsets, which is where most tracking happens. Iteration 1 already showed that coarser spacing near the centre line does not help. The draft does not weigh this loss of resolution.

5. kd=1.0 is large for the sensor scale. One turn unit is 350 PWM.
